preconditions.expression: t == int(stdin.split()[0]) and t >= 1 and t <= 50000
preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 50000) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(2 <= n <= 10**5 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.strip() and (n := int(line.split()[0])) is not None)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line after t is an integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) representing the number of sets.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) >= 2 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.strip())
preconditions.description: Each set description line starts with k_i (2 ≤ k_i ≤ 10^5) followed by k_i distinct integers (1 ≤ a_{i,j} ≤ 10^9).

preconditions.expression: sum(int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.strip()) <= 2 * 10**5
preconditions.description: The total number of elements across all sets in all test cases does not exceed 2 * 10^5.

postconditions.expression: all(len(stdout_line.split()) == 2 and 1 <= int(stdout_line.split()[0]) < int(stdout_line.split()[1]) <= n for stdout_line in stdout.splitlines() if stdout_line.strip() != '-1')
postconditions.description: For each test case with a valid pair of similar sets, the output is two distinct integers (1-based indices) representing the indices of the similar sets.

postconditions.expression: all(stdout_line.strip() == '-1' or (any((set1 := sets[i-1]) and (set2 := sets[j-1]) and len(set1 & set2) >= 2 for i, j in [(int(x), int(y)) for x, y in [line.split() for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip() != '-1']] if i != j)), sets := [set(map(int, line.split()[1:])) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.strip()])
postconditions.description: For each test case, if the output is not '-1', the two sets at the given indices share at least two common elements (i.e., their intersection size is ≥ 2).

postconditions.expression: all(stdout_line.strip() == '-1' or (not any((set1 := sets[i-1]) and (set2 := sets[j-1]) and len(set1 & set2) >= 2 for i, j in [(int(x), int(y)) for x, y in [line.split() for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip() != '-1']] if i != j)) == False, sets := [set(map(int, line.split()[1:])) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.strip()])
postconditions.description: If the output is '-1', there are no two distinct sets in the test case that share at least two common elements.
